title: What is known about 1RB0RA_0RC1LD_0LD0RE_1LB1LE_1RA0LF_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_0RC1LD_0LD0RE_1LB1LE_1RA0LF_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Read in four-cell words (d = 0100, c = 0111), the tape is a list of alternating runs. Near the left the run lengths are nearly all 1 mod 3, further right nearly all multiples of 3, and between them a stretch repeats the lengths 10, 4, 13, 10, 4, 13. Three leftward crossings of runs are proved in Lean. The way the lengths change is not worked out, so halting (F reading a 1) is not ruled out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 46,093 cells have been visited and 22,415 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.665).

claims.title: Leftward crossings
claims.text: (0001)^n D> 0 → D> 0 (0001)^n, (0010)^n C> 0 → C> 0 (0010)^n, (1000)^n B> 1 → B> 1 (1000)^n, for every n.

claims.title: Lengths in base 3
claims.text: At step 199,354,683 (22,052 cells), read as a = 0001, b = 1101, c = 0111, d = 0100, the tape is D>0 a^11 11 b^16 a, then (d^10 c^4 d^13 c^10 d^4 c^13) repeated 12 times, then runs d^16 c^7 d^22 c^28 ... d^149 (lengths 1 mod 3), then groups c^3 d c^k d^3 c d^m with k and m multiples of 3 (36, 21, 9, 42, ...; 66, 51, 57, 69, ...).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when F reads a 1. F is entered from E on a 1 (writing 0, moving left). The sweeps handle runs in a way that keeps the mod-3 pattern in the samples, but this is not proved, and an exception could put F on a 1. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_0RD1LE_0LE0RA_1LC1LA_0LD--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: D, C and B crossing whole runs to the left.
No halt in the C simulator; 46,093 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Runs of two four-cell words
html: The leftmost part (the sqrt-growing side) is a reservoir of 0001. D, C and B cross runs of the one-1 words to the left in one go (proved in Lean).

sections.heading: Base three
html:
The run lengths in the middle part are 1 mod 3 (4, 10, 13, 16, 7, 22, 28, 25, 19, 34, 37, 52, 67, 70). Further right they come in groups c^3 d c^k d^3 c d^m with k and m multiples of 3. So the sweeps seem to read and write the lengths in base 3, much like the splitting by thirds of 1RB1LD_0RC0RF_1LC0LA_0LE1LD_1LA---_0RB0LF in this batch. The repeated stretch d^10 c^4 d^13 c^10 d^4 c^13 grows by whole periods and acts as a wall between the two regimes.

What halting would need. F reading a 1, at a run boundary that breaks the mod-3 pattern. Proving that the pattern is kept would be the first step towards non-halting.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.665).
After 109 steps the tape spans 46,093 cells (30,124 left of the start, 4,183 right), with a density of 1s of 0.486.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A list of runs of the four-cell words 0100 and 0111 whose lengths are nearly all 1 mod 3 (near the left) or multiples of 3 (further right), with a periodic stretch (10, 4, 13, 10, 4, 13, …) between; the lengths further out look irregular.
family: run list in base 3 with a periodic wall
